# Custom rules

Express site-specific risk conditions with a bounded comparison grammar and plan-aware rule configuration.

Source: [site documentation](https://bastionsecurity.io/docs/rules) · platform revision `44c75b5c6715fb9a30b07e2c3ee319e0ac0810b2`.

<a id="create"></a>

## Create a rule

Pro and Enterprise can create custom rules. Use the Rules dashboard or POST /api/rules with a Bearer access token authorized to manage the site. Enabled rules contribute to risk scoring; they do not independently replace your enforcement policy.

**POST /api/rules**

```json
{
  "siteId": "YOUR_SITE_ID",
  "name": "High-value checkout on new account",
  "description": "Adds risk for early high-value orders.",
  "condition": "account.age < 2h AND event.type == \"checkout\" AND event.amount > 200",
  "scoreContribution": 35,
  "enabled": true,
  "category": "payment"
}
```

<a id="grammar"></a>

## Supported grammar

| Element | Supported values |
| --- | --- |
| Fields | event.type, event.amount, account.age, account.riskScore, device.accountCount, ip.accountCount, payment.accountCount. |
| Operators | ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=. |
| Values | Double-quoted strings or nonnegative numeric literals. |
| Time suffixes | h or m for age comparisons, such as 2h or 30m. |
| Composition | Comparisons joined by AND; no OR, JavaScript, functions, or arbitrary expressions. |
| Condition length | At most 1,000 characters. |
| scoreContribution | Number from 0 to 100. |

The stored event type for promo_claim is promo, so use event.type == "promo" in rules. device.accountCount means accounts sharing a device, not devices belonging to one account. GET /api/rules/suggestions returns the accepted fields, operators, and templates.

<a id="manage"></a>

## Manage and test rules

PATCH /api/rules/{id} updates a custom rule. Built-in rules can only be enabled or disabled; their name, condition, and contribution are immutable. Built-in rules cannot be deleted. DELETE removes a custom rule. Plan access is enforced by the API, including after downgrade.

- Begin with monitor mode and review real event evidence.
- Check the matched rule in signals and rulesTriggered after scoring.
- Compare legitimate customer outcomes before switching enforcement.
- Use the site policy threshold and challengeMode for the final action.
